_: WHERE A TASK IS UP TO, once (the owner, 2026-10-26: 'if in todo mode | agent mode | close out mode - are these modes defined well anywhere besides the UI, how the parts of the UI display and what is hidden - we should define this well'). Read by the task page (website/src/stages.js), the server's task detail and the Assistant's CANVAS block (taskuary/stages.py). `rules` decide the stage: the first whose fact holds wins, each side reading the facts its own way - the page from what it is drawing (a live terminal, the white section), the server from the task's rows - and the order is the one both keep. `stages` are the parts each stage draws: `main` the view the task opens on ('work': the agent or Close out is the page, Came from the left drawer; 'task': the task itself is the page, Agent and Close out the right drawer); `shows` what that view holds, in a sentence; `drawer` the drawer and what is in it; `lit` whether that drawer's tab is lit because the next move is inside it; `advisor` where the Advisor's section stands ('main' over the work, 'drawer' in the right drawer, said on its tab, null: none on a closed task); `verbs` the moves the stage is about, by their buttons.json ids, first the one it is for. `section`: which of the desk's three sections in a row - 'from' (1 · Came from), 'agent' (2 · Agent), 'close' (3 · Close out) - the task opens on, the one its next move is in (the owner, 2026-10-27: 'input -> agent/advisor -> close ... on the outside it shows the status of each category and opens up to the one it's up to'). `main` and `drawer` still say a live session's page (the agent the whole width, Came from its left drawer) and the server's and the Assistant's words for a stage.

rules._: an agent's session is open - working, or waiting on you at its prompt
handed to a person: nothing is yours until they answer
closed by its own agent: who closed it and why are the Agent's (trust audit S2, 2026-10-28)
Close out has something of its own: a draft or emails waiting for Send, something that went out, a write-up
an agent finished, stopped or failed, and its Result (or why it failed) is the move
somebody wrote and is owed a reply, nothing drafted yet
a to-do's checklist or a goal's steps are the move
an ask nothing has worked yet - the agent is the move
